text:
Maria: quick thought — for the internal control-plane APIs do we want opaque JSON error envelopes or typed status objects (proto/gRPC-style) that map to HTTP?
Ryan: typed statuses. makes client fallbacks and routing decisions easier (code + stable enum). less guessing.
Sam: +1 for typed statuses, but how does this interact with quota attribution? envelopes can embed route/tenant info so billing doesn’t lose context.
Jon: if we rely on headers for attribution upstream, gateways strip/transform them sometimes. envelopes keep a copy with the response which avoids telemetry gaps.
Lee: SDK ergonomics matter though — our JS/Go clients prefer simple JSON errors (message, details). adding a Status proto forces generated decoding in some clients.
Maria: here's two sketches: envelope approach:
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "QUOTA_EXCEEDED",
    "message": "token quota exceeded for tenant xyz",
    "route_id": "ingest.v2.json",
    "meta": {"usage": 1203} 
  }
}
```
and typed status (proto-mapped to HTTP JSON):
```json
{
  "code": 8, // RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED gRPC code
  "message": "token quota exceeded",
  "details": [{"@type":"type.googleapis.com/redwood.v1.QuotaInfo","tenant_id":"xyz","route":"ingest.v2.json","usage":1203}]
}
```
Ryan: typed status + well-known detail types gives us structured telemetry and avoids reinventing fields. clients can parse details they care about.
Sam: main worry: gateway compatibility. If we ever transit through external proxies that don't preserve gRPC-style details, we lose the typed info.
Jon: proposal: have internal-only endpoints use typed statuses; public-facing endpoints wrap a simple envelope derived from the typed status. Gateway layer does the projection.
Lee: that sounds reasonable. Means SDKs for internal teams can be generated against the proto; external clients get stable JSON.
Maria: UX question for rollouts — how do we migrate? Can we do a canary where the gateway emits both payloads for a window?
Ryan: yes: dual-write approach in gateway v2 — include X-Redwood-Error-Proto header and keep envelope body. Clients can read header and parse details if present.
Sam: that helps telemetry too: our ingest pipeline can prefer proto-details when header present and fall back to envelope fields.
Jon: small nit: need to add signature/hmac for route info in envelope if we rely on it for billing, otherwise untrusted clients could spoof.
Lee: re: SDKs — add helper that normalizes both forms into a single Error object. That will hide complexity from most app authors.
Maria: ok action items: 1) draft proto for QuotaInfo + ErrorDetails (Ryan) 2) gateway change to emit both body forms + X-Redwood-Error-Proto header for canary (Jon/Sam) 3) SDK normalization helper (Lee) 4) docs + console telemetry mapping (Maria).
Jon: +1. I'll start a gateway spike branch.
Ryan: I'll sketch the proto and post a short RFC.
Lee: I'll add the error-normalizer to the JS SDK and a feature flag.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for gateway/error-projection v2 -> 3 hosts (canary). :rocket:
Maria: sweet — we'll sync in next standup. Thanks! :thumbsup:
